metaDescription: Six string trimmers under $100 compared: Greenworks 24V and 40V, BLACK+DECKER 40V MAX, a folding 20V and corded options, by torque, kit and platform.
expertTake: The Greenworks 24V kit is the best ready-to-use trimmer here because the battery and charger are included and the shaft telescopes. The BLACK+DECKER corded 6.5 amp is the value pick for anyone near an outlet. Be careful with the two bare-tool 40V listings: they only make sense if you already own the matching battery. Check the live price and kit contents before ordering.
introParagraphs: This price band is where bigger-name cordless platforms begin to appear, but it is also where listings start to hide the real cost. Some include a battery and charger, others sell only the tool. That is the main trap in this price band.

Reading what is in the box matters more than reading the voltage on the box. Prices move and the $100 cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated, so check the live number and the kit contents before buying. Treat the cap as the price of a complete working kit.

products.name: Greenworks 24V 12-Inch Cordless Trimmer 2.0Ah Kit
products.description:
Greenworks supplies a 2.0Ah battery and charger with this 24V trimmer, so it works out of the box. The aluminum shaft telescopes to fit your height, which is a real comfort feature in a class where many trimmers have a fixed length. A button switches between trimming and edging, and the head pivots to follow sloped ground and tree roots.

The 12-inch swath is typical for a cordless of this size. A single 2Ah pack is modest, so runtime suits a small yard of fifteen to thirty minutes of work. Compared with the folding 20V model, it has a better-known brand and an adjustable shaft, but only one battery.

Because Greenworks sells a broad 24V range, the pack can be shared with a blower or other tools, which lowers the real cost over time. Store the battery indoors and replace the line before it wears short. A good routine is to run the battery down on a job and then charge it fully, rather than topping it up repeatedly. Keep the pivot head locked while trimming so the angle does not drift.
products.bestFor: First-time cordless owners with a small to medium yard.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 6.5A Corded 2-in-1 String Trimmer Edger
products.description:
This corded trimmer relies on a 6.5 amp motor and a Powerdrive transmission to put torque where it counts. EASYFEED advances line with a push of a button, and the head rotates to a wheeled edge guide for sidewalk work. It never runs out of charge.

Compared with the Greenworks, it is more powerful for the money and has unlimited runtime, but you need an outdoor cord and a nearby outlet. Compared with the folding 20V, it has a bigger motor and a longer track record.

A corded trimmer from a mainstream brand is also easy to repair and replace spools for. Coil the cord loosely and inspect it often. The push-button feed saves bumping the head on concrete, which also saves the housing from scuffs. Wear eye protection, since a 6.5 amp head throws gravel hard.
products.bestFor: Corded value for yards within cord reach.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 40V MAX 13-Inch Trimmer Edger Bare Tool
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER 40V MAX adds a power command dial that lets you select maximum strength for thick grass or save charge on light work, a feature the cheaper cordless units lack. A Powerdrive transmission boosts torque at the head and the swath is 13 inches. The listing is based on a robust 40V lithium-ion battery that you must confirm is included.

If you already own a 40V MAX battery from another tool, it is among the best tools in this guide. If you do not, the missing battery and charger can double the real cost, so compare it only on a complete-kit basis. Against the Greenworks 24V it has more power and a dial; against the corded 6.5 amp unit it adds freedom.

Keep the pack indoors and use the lower power setting for light edging to extend runtime. Start on the high setting for tall growth and drop it for edges, which stretches the pack. Mark your battery with the date you bought it so you can judge its age.
products.bestFor: Owners of the 40V MAX platform wanting variable power.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 12-Inch Cordless Trimmer Bare Tool
products.description:
The Greenworks 40V trimmer is listed explicitly without a battery or charger. It uses .065-inch line with an auto-feed head and a variable-speed trigger that lets you ease off near flowerbeds and open up for thick grass.

As a bare tool it is attractive only if you already own 40V Greenworks batteries. If you do, it is a capable, well-supported tool. If you do not, you must add a battery and charger, which pushes the total beyond the cap.

Compared with the Greenworks 24V kit, it is stronger but incomplete. Store the tool dry and keep spare line. Because the pack is separate, buy a spare if you plan to trim for more than twenty minutes. Check that the platform sells the other tools you may want, such as a blower.

products.name: 20V Folding-Shaft Cordless String Trimmer Two 2Ah
products.description:
This 20V trimmer has a shaft that folds 180 degrees in three ways for vertical storage, a handy feature for small garages. A 9,500 RPM motor and intelligent auto-feed that detects line length are the other selling points, and two 2Ah batteries are included.

Its storage trick makes it easy to put away in a closet. Compared with the Greenworks 24V, it ships with two batteries but has a lesser-known brand and no telescoping shaft.

The folding joint is a mechanical weak point, so check that it locks firmly each time you open it. Make sure the folding joint clicks fully into place before pulling the trigger, and wipe grass out of the hinge. Store it upright on its hook and keep batteries elsewhere.
cons: Folding joint is a wear point

products.name: 20V Lightweight Cordless Trimmer Edger Two 2Ah 3.5 lb
products.description:
At 3.5 pounds this is the lightest cordless in the guide. It ships with two 2Ah batteries and offers a 12-inch swath with trimmer, edger and weed cutter modes.

It is the lightest to hold but the weakest on thick growth. Compared with the folding model, it is lighter but less storage friendly.

Good for a tiny yard. It is the right tool for older users or anyone whose wrists tire quickly. Do not use it for dense brush, where the light motor will stall and the packs will drain.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Greenworks 24V includes a 2Ah battery and charger, while the Greenworks 40V is listed without them. A bare-tool price looks lower but a 40V battery and charger can cost as much as the tool. Add the missing parts before comparing. A quick way to compare is to tally the cost of battery, charger and tool together. Do not forget the charger.

24V and 20V platforms are light-duty, 40V is stronger and more expensive. The BLACK+DECKER 40V MAX adds a power dial. If you already own a 40V battery, go that way, otherwise a complete 24V kit is easier. Check that the same pack fits a blower or hedge trimmer before buying into a platform. Voltage names differ between brands.

A power command dial on the BLACK+DECKER or a variable trigger on the Greenworks 40V lets you trade strength for runtime. Light edging does not need full power, and a dial can extend a battery by a third. Use the low setting for edging around flowerbeds. It is easy to try in store.

The Greenworks 24V telescopes and the 20V folds. A telescoping shaft fits more users, and a folding shaft saves space. Both add joints that can loosen over time. Adjust the shaft so your arms are slightly bent when you hold the grips. Joints loosen with use.

The BLACK+DECKER 6.5 amp costs less than most cordless kits, never runs flat and is stronger than the 20V units. It requires an outlet within cord reach. Corded tools are also the easiest to repair, since parts are simple. Cord gauge matters.

A 13 inch swath cuts faster but demands torque. Budget 20V motors at 9,500 RPM cut grass cleanly but bog in thick weeds. Choose the platform with the torque for your growth. Cut tall weeds in layers, top first, to avoid stalling the motor. Wet grass is heavier.

howToChoose.intro: Start from what you already own, since that changes which listing is a bargain.
Tiers are relative and assume you buy a complete kit.

cards.label: Kit
cards.text: The Greenworks 24V and both 20V trimmers include batteries. They are ready to use. You can start trimming within minutes of unboxing.

cards.label: Bare tool
cards.text: The Greenworks 40V is sold without one. It only saves money if you already own the packs. Confirm the battery cost before you click buy.

howToChoose.note: Count the battery cost before judging a price.

howToChoose.intro: Torque and trigger control matter more than headline voltage.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A pivoting head and an adjustable shaft to keep the line level on a slope. Keep the head angled slightly to follow the slope.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Greenworks 24V pivots and telescopes, making it the best fit. A pivot button lets you change angle without tools.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a big yard. Move to a 56V or gas trimmer. A stronger platform also runs cooler.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have a small patch. The corded unit is enough. Put the savings into spare line.

maintenance.why: Short line strains the motor. It is a one-minute habit that prevents most breakdowns. Write the line size on the head.
Packed grass overheats the spool. It is a one-minute habit that prevents most breakdowns. A stiff brush clears it quickly.
Cold reduces capacity. It is a one-minute habit that prevents most breakdowns. Keep them at half charge.
Telescoping and folding joints loosen. It is a one-minute habit that prevents most breakdowns. Tighten the knob by hand.
Nicks are a hazard. It is a one-minute habit that prevents most breakdowns. Replace damaged cords immediately.

faq.a: For small yards, yes. For thick weeds, choose 40V or corded. If you want more torque, move up a platform. Buy once, and buy the platform you will keep.
A tool sold without battery or charger. Add the battery cost to your comparison before you commit. Look for the words battery and charger included.
Corded for power and price, cordless for freedom. A corded unit also needs a decent extension cord. Short extension cords carry less voltage drop.

faq.q: How long does a 2Ah battery last?
faq.a: About 15 to 30 minutes of light trimming. Cold packs deliver less. Two packs double the working time.
Yes, it saves charge on light work. Try it on the lower setting first. It also reduces the load on the motor.
Keep the head off the ground and clear wrapped material with the power off. Replace the line before the next session. Never trim with a loose guard.
